---
title: "Geoms"
---

Each geom adds a layer. Every geom method accepts these arguments, and the [Geoms API](reference-geoms.qmd) lists the rest for each geom.

| Argument | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `aes:` | mappings for this layer only |
| `data:` | data for this layer only |
| `inheritAes: false` | ignores the plot's mappings |
| `filter:` | a Vega expression, or a selection such as `['param' => 'brush']` |
| `alpha`, `color`, `fill`, `size`, `linewidth`, `linetype`, `shape` | fixed styles, by their ggplot2 names |
| any Vega-Lite mark property | passed through, such as `strokeWidth: 2` |

- **`color` and `fill`.** As in ggplot2, `color` is the outline of bars, areas, and tiles, and `fill` is their interior. For points, lines, and text, `color` is the main color.
- **`linetype`.** ggplot2's names (`dashed`, `dotted`, `dotdash`, `longdash`, `twodash`), hex dash strings such as `'44'`, or a dash array.

## Distributions

`histogram()` bins a continuous variable. `bins:` sets the maximum number of bins, and Vega-Lite chooses rounded boundaries. `binwidth:` sets the width exactly and `boundary:` anchors the bins.

{{< include _generated/geom-histogram.md >}}

`density()` draws a kernel density estimate per group with Vega-Lite's density transform. `bw:` sets the bandwidth. `adjust:` multiplies a bandwidth computed with R's `bw.nrd0` rule. Mapping `fill` draws filled areas; otherwise the densities are lines.

{{< include _generated/geom-density.md >}}

`boxplot()` draws Tukey boxplots with whiskers at `coef:` interquartile ranges. Points layered on top show the raw data, here with `jitter()`.

`jitter()`, or `point(jitter:)`, moves points by up to `width:` and `height:`: a share of a band on a discrete axis, or data units on a continuous one.

- **Without a seed,** the browser draws the offsets with Vega's `random()`, so the points move on every render.
- **With `seed:`,** the offsets are drawn in PHP and embedded, so every render and export places the points the same way. A seed needs inline data.

{{< include _generated/geom-boxplot.md >}}

`violin()` draws a kernel density of y for each level of a discrete x, and layers with boxplots and points on the same axis.

- **Width.** Every violin has the same maximum width, `width:` as a share of the band.
- **Density.** For inline data, each group's density is computed in PHP with its own bandwidth (`bw:`, or R's `bw.nrd0` times `adjust:`) at `n:` points (200 by default) across the group's range.
- **Groups.** `position: 'dodge'` places groups side by side within the band.

{{< include _generated/geom-violin.md >}}

`ecdf()`, `freqpoly()`, `qq()`, `qqLine()`, and `rug()` complete the set.

## Amounts

`bar()` counts rows per level of x when y is unmapped, and `col()` draws the y values. `position:` is `stack` (the default), `dodge`, `fill` (stacked to 100%), or `identity`.

{{< include _generated/geom-bars.md >}}

`col()` with `xmin` and `xmax` mapped draws precomputed bins. `tile()` and `rect()` draw heatmaps and rectangles, and `bin2d()` counts points in a two-dimensional grid.

{{< include _generated/geom-tile.md >}}

## Lines and areas

`line()` connects points in order of x. `path()` connects them in data order, and `step()` draws stairsteps. `area()` fills from zero and stacks by `fill`, and `ribbon()` fills between `ymin` and `ymax`.

{{< include _generated/geom-line-area.md >}}

## Intervals

`errorbar()`, `linerange()`, and `pointrange()` draw intervals from `ymin` to `ymax`. With `xmin` and `xmax` they are horizontal. `position: 'dodge'` places groups side by side, which the [coefficient plots](statistics.qmd) use to compare models.

{{< include _generated/geom-intervals.md >}}

## Reference lines

`hline()` and `vline()` draw rules at fixed values, at every value of a list, or at a mapped `yintercept` or `xintercept` field. `abline()` draws `y = intercept + slope * x` across the range of the data.

{{< include _generated/geom-reference.md >}}

## Text

`text()` and `label()` draw the `label` aesthetic. `hjust`, `vjust`, and `angle` follow ggplot2: `angle` turns text counterclockwise. `nudgeX` and `nudgeY` move labels in pixels.

{{< include _generated/geom-text.md >}}

## Fitted curves

`smooth()` fits a curve per group and, for inline data, draws a pointwise confidence band for the mean at `level:`, as ggplot2's `geom_smooth()` does. The band is not a prediction interval for individual points. The default method is loess, a local quadratic fit over the nearest `span:` share of the points (0.75 by default), computed in PHP as R's `loess()` with `surface = "direct"`. ggplot2 interpolates the loess surface instead, so its curve can differ slightly.

{{< include _generated/geom-smooth-loess.md >}}

- **Polynomials.** `method: 'lm'`, `'quad'`, and `'poly'` (with `order:`) fit by least squares in PHP, with bands from R's `predict(fit, interval = "confidence")` formula.
- **In the browser.** `se: false` and the methods `log`, `exp`, and `pow` use Vega-Lite's regression and loess transforms, without a band.
- **Cost of a loess band.** The band costs O(n²) in PHP. For the 234 points of `mpg` it takes about 66 ms to build on the benchmark machine, against under 1 ms for an lm band ([Small plots](https://phiz.phpstats.org/benchmarks/small-plot-build)). `se: false` leaves the curve to Vega-Lite's transform in the browser.
- **Large data.** Above 3,000 rows, loess defaults to the browser. `se: true` computes the band anyway.

{{< include _generated/geom-smooth.md >}}

`curve()` draws a PHP function over a range, as ggplot2's `geom_function()` does.

{{< include _generated/geom-curve.md >}}

## Summaries

`summary()` summarizes y at each value of x and draws the result with another geom, as ggplot2's `stat_summary()` does. `funData:` returns the middle and the range together:

| `funData:` | Middle | Range | Option |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mean_se` (default) | mean | ± 1 standard error | `funArgs: ['mult' => 2]` |
| `mean_cl_normal` | mean | t confidence interval | `funArgs: ['conf' => 0.9]` |
| `mean_sdl` | mean | ± 2 standard deviations | |
| `median_hilow` | median | outer quantiles at `conf` (0.95) | |

- **Custom summaries.** A callable returning `[y, ymin, ymax]` replaces `funData:`. `fun:`, `funMin:`, and `funMax:` set the parts separately ([Geoms API](reference-geoms.qmd#summary)).
- **Drawing.** `geom:` is `pointrange` (default), `errorbar`, `linerange`, `crossbar`, `point`, `line`, `col`, `area`, or `ribbon`.
- **Orientation.** With a discrete y and a continuous x, x is summarized at each y.

{{< include _generated/geom-summary.md >}}

`crossbar()` draws a box from `ymin` to `ymax` with a line at `y`, and it works with `summary()` and `position: 'dodge'`.

{{< include _generated/geom-crossbar.md >}}

`count()` draws a point at each distinct x and y, sized by the number of rows there, as `geom_count()` does.

`ellipse()` draws a confidence ellipse per group, as `stat_ellipse()` does. `type: 't'` (the default) fits a multivariate t distribution with MASS's `cov.trob()`, `'norm'` uses the sample covariance, and `'euclid'` draws a circle of radius `level`. `geom: 'polygon'` fills them.

{{< include _generated/geom-ellipse.md >}}

## Two-dimensional densities and contours

`density2d()` estimates a bivariate kernel density on a 100 × 100 grid and draws its contour lines, as `geom_density_2d()` does. The density is MASS's `kde2d()` with `bandwidth.nrd()` bandwidths, computed in PHP, and the contour levels are R's `pretty()` over the range of the density. `h:` sets the bandwidths, `adjust:` multiplies them, and `bins:`, `binwidth:`, or `breaks:` set the levels. Mapping `color: 'level'` colors each line by its level. Mapping `color` to a field estimates one density per group.

{{< include _generated/geom-density2d.md >}}

`density2dFilled()` fills the bands between consecutive levels and labels them as ggplot2 does, with the viridis palette. `contourVar: 'ndensity'` scales each group's density to a maximum of 1, and `'count'` multiplies it by the group's size.

{{< include _generated/geom-density2d-filled.md >}}

`contour()` and `contourFilled()` draw the same lines and bands for a `z` field on a regular grid of `x` and `y`, as `geom_contour()` and `geom_contour_filled()` do. phiz traces the contours in PHP with marching squares.

{{< include _generated/geom-contour.md >}}

`polygon()` fills the shape through each group's points in data order. Rows with null `x` and `y` start a new ring in the same group, and a ring drawn in the opposite direction cuts a hole.

## Annotations

`annotate()` adds a layer from fixed values rather than data, as ggplot2's `annotate()` does. It draws `text`, `label`, `point`, `segment`, `rect`, `rule`, `pointrange`, `linerange`, `errorbar`, or `crossbar`. Positions can be single values or lists, and `-INF` and `INF` reach the edges of the panel. Annotations ignore the plot's mappings, keep its axis titles, and appear in every facet panel.

{{< include _generated/geom-annotate.md >}}

## Raw layers

`layer()` adds any Vega-Lite layer as given, and `geom()` adds a geom by name with explicit parameter and style arrays.

## Agreement with R

The smoothing, density, contour, ellipse, and summary computations are compared with R on the bundled datasets: see [Smoothing](https://phiz.phpstats.org/verification/r-smoothing) and [Distributions and contours](https://phiz.phpstats.org/verification/r-distributions) for each comparison, its tolerance, and its result.
